messages:
acme-payments: Hey @support, VAT still appears on our invoice INV-2026-042 even though we submitted an EU exemption ID in the portal. Portal showed a 504/Gateway timeout during the VIES check. Screenshot: https://acme.example/screenshot.png

billing-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-10982 — an agent will follow up within 24h :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: Thanks — can you paste the EU VAT number you entered (include country code) and attach the resale certificate PDF if you have it?

acme-payments: VAT number used: DE123456789. The portal VIES lookup returned a timeout (504) but we got a confirmation page that the upload succeeded. Uploading PDF now: https://acme.example/resale-cert.pdf

maria: Got it. FYI VIES timeouts can trigger an automatic rejection path in the portal. If you can confirm the legal entity name on the invoice we can do a manual validation and proceed with a credit. What's the exact invoiced entity name?

acme-payments: Invoiced as: Acme Payments GmbH — that matches registration docs. We just uploaded the business registration and resale cert in the ticket.

jason-billing: Looping in billing ops @oliver — manual override checklist for SUP-10982: 1) verify PDF matches VAT number and registered company name, 2) set invoice status to "exempt-manual" in billing dashboard, 3) issue credit note, 4) reissue invoice net of VAT. Keep the VIES attempt logs attached for audit.

oliver: On it. I'll validate the PDF and run the manual flow. Quick question for legal: do we need the buyer declaration under Article 138 or is the resale cert + registration document sufficient?

maria: Legal: resale certificate + company reg extract + matching VAT number is sufficient for a manual override. If VIES later reports valid we can flip the automation back but preserve the audit trail. @acme-payments we have what we need and will process the credit — expect credit note within 48h :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: Credit note CN-2026-077 issued for INV-2026-042. Reference: SUP-10982. :package:
